missingInputs.description: No official R4-to-R6 diff page or change log was supplied or reviewed for RelatedPerson.
No terminology server expansion was available for http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-PersonalRelationshipRoleType or for version-specific relationship/language value sets.
The generated narrative embedded in the R6 StructureDefinition was available, but the full rendered R4 and R6 specification pages and ballot change notes were not separately reviewed.
No official R4/R6 ConceptMap was available for migrating RelatedPerson.relationship content into RelatedPerson.relationship versus RelatedPerson.role.

scope.scopeNotesMd: This report compares the local `RelatedPerson` resource definition in R4 4.0.1 with the same canonical StructureDefinition in the R6 6.0.0-ballot4 package. I treated elements present in the RelatedPerson differential as local, including the nested `RelatedPerson.communication` backbone. Changes inherited only from `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, `BackboneElement`, or reused datatypes are intentionally excluded from `findings[]` even when visible in the RelatedPerson snapshot.
outOfScope: Inherited `Resource.language` binding changed from preferred Common Languages to required All Languages; this belongs to the Resource/base artifact analysis, not RelatedPerson.
Inherited `DomainResource.modifierExtension` summary flag differs in the snapshot; this belongs to DomainResource/base artifact analysis.
Inherited DomainResource containment constraints and Element `ele-1` wording/expression changes are excluded from local findings.
Changes inside reused datatypes such as Identifier, HumanName, ContactPoint, Address, Attachment, Period, CodeableConcept, Reference, and Meta were not assessed here.
SearchParameters, operations, CapabilityStatements, profiles, examples, and implementation-guide-specific rules were not assessed except where the core StructureDefinition references a binding.
The THO value set `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-PersonalRelationshipRoleType` was referenced by R6 but not present as a local ValueSet artifact in the supplied R6 core package.

narrativeReportMd:
# RelatedPerson R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
RelatedPerson keeps the same canonical identity and has no local element removals, local cardinality tightening, type removals, or reference-target changes. The material local risks are concentrated in terminology and semantics: `communication.language` now has a required BCP-47 language binding, and the broad R4 `relationship` concept is split in R6 into personal `relationship` and functional `role`.

## Scope
This report owns changes defined locally on RelatedPerson and its local `communication` backbone. Inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element changes are documented as out of scope rather than duplicated as RelatedPerson findings.

## Main migration themes
The main R4-to-R6 validation break is stricter terminology validation for `RelatedPerson.communication.language`. The main semantic migration is to classify existing `relationship` codings into personal relationships that remain on `relationship` versus functional roles that move to the new `role` element. The main R6-to-R4 round-trip issue is that `RelatedPerson.role` has no native R4 element.

## Highest-impact findings
- `RelatedPerson.communication.language` binding strength increased from preferred to required, so text-only or local-code language concepts that were acceptable in R4 can fail strict R6 validation.
- `RelatedPerson.role` was added for functional relationships; valid R6 role data is not natively representable in R4.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for relationship-code migration and for systems that used RelatedPerson telecom or identifiers to represent application user identities. The exact terminology impact of the personal relationship value set should be confirmed with a terminology expansion.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The language binding change could have been softened with warnings or profile guidance, but the likely goal is stronger interoperability. The relationship/role split is semantically cleaner, but a less disruptive path would have preserved the old broad relationship semantics while adding `role` as an optional refinement.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the Resource/DomainResource base reports for inherited binding and summary-flag changes, and obtain a terminology expansion or ConceptMap for relationship-to-role migration.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: RelatedPerson has one clear local hard validation risk (`communication.language` required binding), one high R6-to-R4 round-trip risk (`role` added), and a significant semantic split of `relationship` into personal relationship versus functional role. Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas and medium for exact terminology-code impact without expansions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should first validate all `RelatedPerson.communication.language` values against BCP-47 and replace text-only/local language concepts with `urn:ietf:bcp:47` codings where possible. Second, classify each R4 `relationship` coding: personal relationships remain on `relationship`; functional contacts such as employer, emergency contact, interpreter, guarantor, or power of attorney should move to R6 `role`. Third, R6-to-R4 transforms need an extension or lossy policy for `role` because R4 has no native element.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the local element set, cardinalities, types, reference targets, bindings, and flags were compared because both local StructureDefinitions and package index entries were inspected. Confidence is lower for exact code-level relationship migration because the R6 personal relationship value set is referenced from terminology.hl7.org but was not present as a local ValueSet to expand.

findings.title: RelatedPerson.communication.language binding strengthened from preferred Common Languages to required All Languages

oldState.summary: R4 used a preferred binding to Common Languages, with an ElementDefinition maxValueSet extension pointing to All Languages.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 element's primary binding was preferred, so use of local codes or text-only CodeableConcepts was not a base conformance error. The R4 binding also carried a maxValueSet extension for All Languages, which some tooling may already have treated as an upper bound.

semanticText.short: The language which can be used to communicate with the patient about his or her health
semanticText.comment: Not all systems actually code this but instead have it as free text. Hence CodeableConcept instead of code as the data type.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a communication language was mandatory inside each `communication` backbone entry, but the terminology binding was only preferred. Implementations could represent a language with free text or a local code without failing the base binding.

newState.summary: R6 uses a required binding to All Languages version 6.0.0-ballot4 and keeps Common Languages only as a starter additional binding.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: All Languages is based on BCP-47 (`urn:ietf:bcp:47`). R6 Common Languages remains available as a starter binding and locally contains more listed common codes than R4, but it is no longer the required conformance set.

semanticText.short: The language which can be used to communicate with the related person about the patient's health
semanticText.definition: The language which may be used to communicate with the individual.
semanticText.comment: The language is commonly represented using the ISO-639-1 alpha code in lower case for the language, optionally followed by a hyphen and the ISO-3166-1 alpha code for the region in upper case.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, each `communication.language` must satisfy a required BCP-47 language value set. The datatype remains `CodeableConcept`, but strict validators now need a code from the required language value set rather than merely encouraging common language codes.

facts.note: R6 preserves Common Languages as starter guidance rather than as the primary binding.
The R4 maxValueSet extension reduces the practical break for systems already enforcing it, but the base binding strength still changed from preferred to required.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct terminology-validation break for strict R6 validation. An R4 instance can contain `communication.language` as text-only or with a local/non-BCP-47 code and still satisfy the R4 preferred binding, but the same value can fail R6 required binding validation. Runtime risk is medium because generated models do not change shape, but validators, test suites, and terminology-dependent workflows can start rejecting migrated data.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Language data can affect interpreter needs and patient-family communication. Rejecting or dropping language entries during migration can create operational access risks even though this is not a clinical-content field.

justification.inferredGoal: Make communication languages consistently computable as BCP-47 language tags.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a non-required base binding to BCP-47/All Languages and add base warning or best-practice guidance for interoperable exchanges.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal, making communication languages reliably computable as BCP-47 tags, is reasonable for interoperability and operational language-access workflows. A less-breaking base design could have retained a preferred/non-required binding with stronger warnings, but that only encourages cleanup; it does not give R6 validators and exchange partners the same assurance that every `communication.language` has an allowed language tag. Given that material tradeoff, the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept the base binding non-required, perhaps pointing it at All Languages/BCP-47 and adding a warning-level invariant or best-practice note. That would preserve R4-valid text-only and local-coded `CodeableConcept` values. It is only a partial alternative because profile guidance or migration tooling is not a base-design substitute, and the base specification would still permit non-computable language values.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves text-only and local-coded R4 instances, but does not guarantee computable language tags in all base R6 data.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred and valueSet is Common Languages.
R4 also declares a maximum value set of All Languages.
R6 binding strength is required and valueSet is All Languages version 6.0.0-ballot4.
R6 All Languages includes all codes from BCP-47.

examples.examplesMd: The old example is an illustrative fragment with the required `patient` element included. It shows a text-only `CodeableConcept` that R4 could accept under a preferred binding but that is likely to fail strict R6 required-binding validation.

findings.narrativeMd: `RelatedPerson.communication.language` did not change cardinality or datatype, but its binding became substantially stricter. This matters because real systems often store communication language as display text or local codes. Those instances may parse successfully in R6 but fail terminology validation unless migrated to BCP-47 codings such as `urn:ietf:bcp:47#es`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances can become R6-invalid when a `communication` entry has no coding from the required All Languages value set. Valid R6 content remains structurally representable in R4 because the element and datatype already existed, although R4 validators will treat the binding as preferred rather than required.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all RelatedPerson communication entries. Where language is text-only or local-coded, map it to a BCP-47 code and retain the original text when useful. Add tests for text-only, local-code, common BCP-47, regional BCP-47, and sign-language tags. If mapping cannot be automated safely, queue records for manual review rather than dropping the communication entry.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The interoperability goal could have been met less disruptively with a preferred binding plus a best-practice warning or profile. The R6 required binding is cleaner for validators and exchange partners, but it moves cleanup of legacy language data into the base-version migration path.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm exact validator behavior for CodeableConcept text-only values under a required binding with the validator version used by the adopting program.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 turns `RelatedPerson.communication.language` from a preferred Common Languages binding into a required All Languages/BCP-47 binding while leaving the path, cardinality, and `CodeableConcept` type unchanged. That is a real old-valid/new-invalid risk for R4 data that used only text or local language codes, especially in strict terminology-validation pipelines. The affected data is operationally important for communicating with the related person and arranging language access, but the R6 goal of ensuring computable language tags is directly related to that same operational need. A softer design would reduce migration burden but would not give receivers a base-level guarantee that language values are machine-processable.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition RelatedPerson.communication.language: 1..1 CodeableConcept with preferred binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/languages and maxValueSet extension to all-languages.

R6 StructureDefinition RelatedPerson.communication.language: 1..1 CodeableConcept with required binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-languages|6.0.0-ballot4 and Common Languages retained only as a starter binding.
R4/R6 ValueSet-all-languages compose includes urn:ietf:bcp:47; R4 ValueSet-languages is only a common-language subset.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 RelatedPerson is FMM 2 and trial-use, so the stability expectation is neutral rather than normative; the hard validation mechanism matters, but the maturity level lowers the case for revisiting a proportionate terminology cleanup.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 text-only or locally coded communication language CodeableConcept values could pass the preferred binding but fail strict R6 required BCP-47 binding validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking base design exists: keep the binding preferred or make it non-required against All Languages with a best-practice warning. That would preserve more R4 instances, but it materially weakens the R6 goal because base R6 data could still contain non-computable language values.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative assessment; I agree there is a direct validation break, but judge it proportionate because the stronger binding serves the interoperability goal.

findings.title: RelatedPerson.relationship narrowed to personal relationships while functional relationships move to RelatedPerson.role

oldState.summary: R4 relationship represented the nature of the relationship between patient and related person with a preferred binding to Patient Relationship Type.

binding.description: The nature of the relationship between a patient and the related person.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 Patient Relationship Type included all of v2-0131 and a v3 RoleCode filter for `_PersonalRelationshipRoleType`, so the old binding mixed broad contact/relationship concepts.

semanticText.definition: The nature of the relationship between a patient and the related person.
semanticText.requirements: We need to know the relationship with the patient since it influences the interpretation of the information attributed to this person.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used one repeating `relationship` element for the relationship between the patient and the related person, without a local split between personal relationships and functional contact roles.

newState.summary: R6 relationship is explicitly personal, with functional relationships represented by the new RelatedPerson.role element.

binding.description: The nature of the personal relationship between a patient and the related person.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 personal relationship value set is referenced from terminology.hl7.org and was not present as a local package artifact to expand.

semanticText.short: The personal relationship of the related person to the patient
semanticText.definition: The nature of the personal relationship between the related person and the patient.
semanticText.comment: This property is for personal relationships. Functional relationships are represented in `RelatedPerson.role`.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same path but narrows its meaning to personal relationships. It also documents relationship directionality from RelatedPerson to Patient, with examples such as parent or mother.

facts.oldValue: The nature of the relationship between a patient and the related person.
facts.newValue: The nature of the personal relationship between the related person and the patient.

facts.note: The binding remains preferred, so this is primarily semantic/interoperability risk rather than a direct validation failure.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged; the change is a local meaning and binding shift, paired with the new sibling `RelatedPerson.role`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding remains preferred and the datatype/cardinality are unchanged, existing R4 instances are not directly invalidated by base structural validation. The break is semantic: R4 data that used `relationship` for functional roles can be misinterpreted in R6 unless moved to `role`. Code that switches on relationship codes or assumes all relationship concepts live in one property must be updated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misclassifying a functional contact role as a personal relationship can affect contact prioritization, emergency contact workflows, guarantor/billing workflows, or legal-representative handling.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate personal kinship relationships from functional care, contact, legal, or administrative roles.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `role` while retaining broad R4 `relationship` semantics for a transition period and recommending, but not requiring, the split.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating personal relationships from functional roles is a reasonable R6 modeling goal because those concepts drive different clinical, administrative, legal, and contact workflows. The less-breaking path of keeping `relationship` broad while adding `role` would preserve most R4 data semantically, but it would also create long-lived duplicate representations for the same fact and make consumers unable to trust that functional roles have moved to `role`. Those material interoperability costs support a `Probably justified` verdict.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base-design alternative would have added optional `RelatedPerson.role` but kept `RelatedPerson.relationship` defined broadly, with deprecation or preference text for placing functional relationships in `role`. This avoids reclassifying existing R4 `relationship` data immediately. The downside is validation and interpretation ambiguity: the same functional relationship could appear in either field indefinitely, and deprecated same-resource representations tend to accumulate rather than disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy semantics, but leaves personal and functional concepts duplicated in the same resource and may prevent the split from ever becoming reliable.

evidence.detail: R4 relationship definition is broad and binding uses Patient Relationship Type.
evidence.quote: The nature of the relationship between a patient and the related person.

evidence.detail: R6 relationship definition is personal and directs functional relationships to role.
evidence.quote: This property is for personal relationships. Functional relationships are represented in `RelatedPerson.role`.

evidence.detail: R6 relationship uses the THO PersonalRelationshipRoleType value set.
R6 Patient Relationship Type now enumerates functional role/contact concepts used by RelatedPerson.role.
evidence.quote: ECON, NOK, GUARD, EMP, GUAR, CAREGIVER, INTPRTER, POWATT

examples.examplesMd: The example shows the semantic migration pattern for a functional relationship. Personal relationship codes such as parent or mother should remain on `relationship`; functional contact roles should move to `role`.

findings.narrativeMd: `RelatedPerson.relationship` is still present, repeatable, and `CodeableConcept`, but it no longer means the same broad thing. In R6 it is specifically the personal relationship from the related person to the patient; functional roles are explicitly modeled in the new `role` element. This can surprise implementers because an unchanged JSON path now carries narrower meaning.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a hard base validation break because the binding remains preferred and no cardinality/type restriction changed. It is a semantic and mapping break: old functional-role content can remain syntactically valid but be placed in the wrong R6 element, while R6 data that uses both personal relationship and functional role cannot be faithfully collapsed into the single R4 relationship element without policy decisions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create a relationship classification table. Keep personal/kinship concepts on `relationship`; map functional, contact, legal, billing, emergency-contact, interpreter, guarantor, employer, or caregiver concepts to `role`. Preserve ambiguous original codings and route them for human review. Regression tests should include one personal relationship, one functional role, and one ambiguous/custom relationship code.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split is semantically justified but not fully backward-compatible because it changes the intended meaning of a pre-existing path. A deprecation period or compatibility profile could have reduced disruption, but would also leave consumers unable to rely on a clean separation in base R6.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A terminology expansion or official ConceptMap is needed before automating large-scale code migration with high confidence.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 keeps `RelatedPerson.relationship` structurally optional and repeating but narrows its meaning to personal relationships, while functional relationships move to the new `RelatedPerson.role` element. Existing R4 instances are not directly rejected by base structural validation because the datatype, cardinality, and preferred binding strength remain permissive. The real migration burden is semantic: systems that placed emergency-contact, guarantor, interpreter, caregiver, or legal-authority concepts in `relationship` need classification and mapping so consumers do not treat functional roles as kinship or personal relationships. The split is a reasonable model improvement, and keeping the old broad semantics indefinitely would make the new role/relationship distinction unreliable.
keyEvidence: R4 RelatedPerson.relationship definition: nature of the relationship between patient and related person, preferred binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/relatedperson-relationshiptype.

R6 RelatedPerson.relationship definition/comment: personal relationship only; functional relationships represented in RelatedPerson.role; preferred binding to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-PersonalRelationshipRoleType.
R6 ValueSet-relatedperson-relationshiptype used by role includes functional/contact concepts such as ECON, NOK, GUARD, GUAR, CAREGIVER, INTPRTER, POWATT, and BILL.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 RelatedPerson is FMM 2 and trial-use, so FMM is neutral. It does not eliminate semantic migration risk, but it makes the burden of preserving the older mixed relationship model lower than it would be for normative content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the same R4 wire path remains accepted, but its intended meaning is narrowed and some codes now belong semantically in RelatedPerson.role.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking design would add `role` but leave `relationship` broad or deprecate functional use gradually. That would preserve legacy interpretation, but it creates duplicate valid homes for the same functional role and prevents R6 consumers from trusting the split.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative assessment; the concern is real but mostly semantic, and the cleaner R6 model has meaningful interoperability benefits.

findings.title: R6 adds RelatedPerson.role for functional relationships with no native R4 counterpart

oldState.narrativeMd: Functional contact roles had to be represented, if at all, using `RelatedPerson.relationship`, extensions, or local conventions.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional repeating RelatedPerson.role for functional relationship roles.

binding.description: The nature of the functional relationship between the patient and the related person.

semanticText.short: The functional role of the related person to the patient
semanticText.definition: The nature of the functional relationship between the patient and the related person.
semanticText.comment: This property is for functional relationships. Personal relationships are represented in `RelatedPerson.relationship`.

newState.narrativeMd: The new R6 element is optional and repeatable, so it does not make old R4 instances invalid. It does create a new first-class representation that older models and R4 payloads do not understand.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional element additions are not R4-to-R6 validation breaks. The risk is R6-to-R4 and runtime/codegen: R4 generated classes do not have a `role` property, strict R4 parsers can reject it as unknown, and tolerant converters can silently drop functional-role data.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping role information can affect emergency contact, interpreter, caregiver, billing, guarantor, or legal-authority workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent functional relationships separately from personal relationships.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: The optional R6 `role` addition is not an R4-to-R6 breaking base-design issue; existing R4 instances remain valid without it.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding an optional, repeating `role` element is a reasonable way to represent functional relationships separately from personal relationships, and it does not invalidate R4 instances during R4-to-R6 migration. The reported risk is mainly R6-to-R4 representability and old-model runtime support, not avoidable R4-to-R6 base breakage. Therefore the backward-compatible-alternative question is not applicable for this finding.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R6 base alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the element is additive and optional. An extension-first or cross-version-backport approach could help R4 systems carry R6 role data, but that is a down-conversion/interoperability mitigation, not a backward-compatible alternative to the R6 base model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 exchange still needs mapping policy, but extensions, backports, or conversion tooling are mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base designs.

evidence.detail: R4 differential has no RelatedPerson.role element.

evidence.quote: The nature of the functional relationship between the patient and the related person.

evidence.detail: R6 role has a preferred binding to Patient Relationship Type.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment is validly shaped for R6 but has no native R4 property for `role`. A converter must either map it into R4 `relationship` with semantic loss, use an extension, or drop it.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `RelatedPerson.role` as a first-class repeating element. This is not a problem for R4-to-R6 validation because it is optional, but it is a material round-trip and codegen issue: R4 clients and schemas do not know the property.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to this addition. Valid R6 instances containing `role` are not cleanly representable in R4. Strict R4 parsers may reject the unknown property, while permissive parsers or lossy converters may discard it.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, move functional relationship codes from `relationship` into `role` where they can be classified confidently. For R6-to-R4, choose a policy: map `role` into R4 `relationship` with an annotation, use a cross-version extension, or reject records where role loss is unacceptable.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The addition is a reasonable model improvement, but no new core element can be backward-compatible for R6-to-R4 consumers. An extension-first design would have been more backward-compatible but less visible and less likely to be implemented consistently.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The new `RelatedPerson.role` element is optional, repeating, and non-modifier, so it does not invalidate R4 RelatedPerson instances during an R4-to-R6 migration. Its compatibility cost is in the reverse or mixed-version direction: R6 data can now carry first-class functional-role information that older R4 models do not have a native property for, so strict R4 parsers may reject it and tolerant converters may drop it. Because this element is the companion to the relationship split and gives functional roles an explicit home, the reverse-version burden appears inherent rather than a sign that the R6 design should be revisited.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has no RelatedPerson.role element.
R6 StructureDefinition adds RelatedPerson.role as 0..* CodeableConcept, isSummary true, isModifier false.
R6 RelatedPerson.role binding is preferred to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/relatedperson-relationshiptype for functional relationships.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 RelatedPerson is FMM 2 and trial-use. That neutral stability level supports treating the additive R6 model change as acceptable, while still acknowledging practical R6-to-R4 conversion loss.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 role data has no native R4 element and can be rejected by strict R4 parsers or lost in down-conversion unless mapped to relationship, extension, or local policy.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No better base R6 design is apparent for R4-to-R6 compatibility because the element is optional and additive. An extension-first or cross-version-extension approach could help older systems, but it would make the functional-role model less visible and is a mitigation rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Not applicable alternative assessment; I agree the addition is not an R4-to-R6 hard break, but the medium concern is limited to reverse or mixed-version exchange.

findings.title: R6 adds user-identity guidance: use identifier type USER, not telecom

oldState.summary: R4 described telecom as contact details and had no local guidance about application user identities.

semanticText.definition: A contact detail for the person, e.g. a telephone number or an email address.
semanticText.comment: Person may have multiple ways to be contacted with different uses or applicable periods.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `telecom` was generic contact information and `identifier` had no local comment about user identity representation.

newState.summary: R6 says systems MAY use identifier with type USER for user identities and DO NOT use telecom properties for user identities.

semanticText.definition: A contact detail for the person, e.g. a telephone number or an email address.
semanticText.comment: DO NOT use .telecom properties to represent user identities.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same structures but adds local conformance guidance separating contact points from user-identity identifiers.

facts.newValue: Systems MAY use identifier for user identities (using the type='USER').
DO NOT use .telecom properties to represent user identities.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a structural validation break, but it can be a conformance and security-model migration issue. Systems that treated e-mail, phone, or other `telecom` values as login/user identifiers now conflict with explicit R6 guidance and should migrate those identities to `identifier` with an appropriate type.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Conflating contact points with user identities can affect account linking, authentication, privacy, and notification workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify the distinction between contact details and account/user identities for security and privacy purposes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use softer base comments that recommend `identifier` type `USER` for account identities without a hard `DO NOT` on `telecom`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying that contact points are not user identities is a reasonable security and privacy goal, and the R6 change does not alter wire shape or make ordinary telecom contact values invalid. A softer base-comment design could have reduced surprise for systems that overloaded email or phone as account identity, but it would also weaken the warning against a risky modeling pattern. Because the remaining breakage is semantic/conformance-level and the safety rationale is plausible, the stronger guidance is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base-design alternative would keep `telecom` comments contact-focused and add milder base guidance on `identifier` saying that account/user identities should preferably be represented with `Identifier` type `USER`, leaving stricter prohibition to security guidance. That preserves more compatibility with legacy account-linking assumptions, but it does not meet the R6 goal as strongly because implementers may continue conflating contact reachability with authenticated identity.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Less disruptive for systems that reused telecom as an account identifier, but weaker and easier-to-miss security/privacy guidance.

evidence.detail: R4 telecom comment only describes multiple ways to contact the person.
evidence.quote: Person may have multiple ways to be contacted with different uses or applicable periods.

evidence.detail: R6 telecom comment prohibits using telecom properties to represent user identities.
evidence.quote: DO NOT use .telecom properties to represent user identities.

evidence.detail: R6 identifier comment allows identifier for user identities using type USER.
evidence.quote: Systems MAY use identifier for user identities (using the type='USER').

examples.examplesMd: The example is conceptual: the exact identifier system and type coding system should follow the implementation's security model and identifier policy.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds explicit guidance that user identities should not be modeled as telecom values and may be modeled as identifiers with type `USER`. This does not invalidate existing JSON by itself, but it can break assumptions in portal, proxy-access, account-linking, or notification integrations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes structurally invalid solely because of this comment change. The compatibility risk appears when R6 conformance reviews, security audits, or business rules reject the old modeling pattern even though the wire representation still parses.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit systems that use RelatedPerson e-mail, phone, or URL contact points as login names, account links, or proxy user identifiers. Move identity semantics into `identifier` with an implementation-approved system/type while retaining telecom only for contactability. Add tests that distinguish contact e-mail from account identifier.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because this is guidance rather than a structural change, the specification could have avoided disruption by keeping the comments unchanged. The added guidance is likely justified by security/privacy clarity, but implementers need to review local account-linking assumptions.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 comment references Security and Privacy guidance not reviewed as a separate narrative page in this report.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds guidance that `telecom` should not be used for user identities and points identity semantics toward `identifier` with type `USER`, but it does not change the `telecom` path, cardinality, type, or ordinary contact-point meaning. Existing phone, email, and URL contact values remain representable. Systems that had overloaded contact details as login or account identifiers should review their security model, but this is a clarification of modeling guidance rather than a structural or terminology compatibility break for RelatedPerson data.
keyEvidence: R4 RelatedPerson.telecom: 0..* ContactPoint, comment describes multiple ways to contact the person and identification help.
R6 RelatedPerson.telecom remains 0..* ContactPoint and adds: DO NOT use .telecom properties to represent user identities.
R6 RelatedPerson.identifier comment says systems MAY use identifier for user identities using type='USER'.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 RelatedPerson is FMM 2 and trial-use, so FMM is neutral. Because the change is guidance-only and not a base instance rejection, maturity does not create a strong revisit concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: no wire-format or validation shape changes; the compatibility effect is limited to systems that treated contact points as user identities despite the contact-oriented datatype.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A softer comment could have been less disruptive for legacy identity-over-telecom conventions, but it would also weaken the security/privacy clarification. Since ordinary contact data is unaffected, no less-breaking base design is needed.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative assessment; I would downgrade this to no meaningful compatibility problem because it is non-computable guidance with a clear security rationale.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R4 and R6 package indexes both identify `StructureDefinition-RelatedPerson.json` with canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/RelatedPerson`, kind `resource`, type `RelatedPerson`, derivation `specialization`, base `DomainResource`, and `abstract=false`.
No local R4 elements were removed. The only local R6 addition is `RelatedPerson.role`, reported as a finding. Inherited snapshot additions/flag changes were excluded by scope.
All pre-existing local RelatedPerson differential elements kept the same min and max cardinalities, including `patient` 1..1, `relationship` 0..*, and `communication.language` 1..1.

No pre-existing local RelatedPerson element changed datatype. `patient` remains `Reference(Patient)`, coded properties remain `CodeableConcept` or `code` as before, and local contact/name/address/photo/period datatypes are unchanged.

Material local binding changes are reported for `relationship` and `communication.language`. `gender` remains required AdministrativeGender with the same four CodeSystem codes (`male`, `female`, `other`, `unknown`) despite a versioned value set URL change.
No new local RelatedPerson-specific invariant was found. Differences in inherited `dom-*`, `ele-1`, or extension constraints are excluded as base-artifact scope.
The local `active` element remains a modifier with the same modifier reason and meaning-when-missing. No newly added local modifier element was found.

Pre-existing local summary flags are unchanged. The new `role` element is summary=true and is covered by its element-addition finding. The inherited `modifierExtension` summary change is out of scope.
No local fixed, pattern, or defaultValue constraints were found on RelatedPerson elements in either version.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex value-limit changes were found.
No local slicing definitions or slice identity changes were found for RelatedPerson.
No local choice element rename, representation change, or primitive/datatype serialization shape change was found. Runtime serializers still need to add support for the new `role` property.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Maturity advanced from draft/trial-use FMM 2 to active/normative FMM 5
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This changes standards maturity metadata rather than instance shape. It can affect governance expectations but does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Organizations may treat normative R6 RelatedPerson semantics as more stable and may tighten review of deviations from base guidance.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 period comment advises separate RelatedPerson instances for non-adjacent periods
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `period` remains optional `0..1 Period`; no validation constraint was added.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that reuse one RelatedPerson record across multiple separated episodes should consider separate instances when modeling R6 data, especially if role/relationship changes over time.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Communication wording now consistently refers to communicating with the related person
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element name, datatype, and cardinality are unchanged. The wording clarifies that the communication language belongs to the related person, not the patient.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review UI labels and documentation that say 'communicate with the patient' when displaying RelatedPerson communication preferences.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Common Languages starter value set lists more common BCP-47 codes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The Common Languages set is an additional starter binding in R6, not the required conformance value set for `communication.language`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The local R6 Common Languages value set listed 93 codes versus 56 in R4, with no removals in the local compose lists. This can improve starter pick lists but should not be treated as the full allowed set.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds interface-pattern mappings and explicit mustSupport=false values
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Mappings and explicit `mustSupport=false` metadata do not alter base instance validity. They can affect tooling documentation or model-analysis outputs but not wire compatibility.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or documentation tooling that surface mappings may show new Interface Pattern mappings for participant/contactable/living-person concepts.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The RelatedPerson snapshot shows inherited `Resource.language` binding strengthened from preferred Common Languages to required All Languages. This is materially relevant to RelatedPerson instances but must be owned by the Resource/base artifact report.
The inherited `modifierExtension` summary flag appears changed in the RelatedPerson snapshot. It is excluded from local findings and should be assessed in the DomainResource report.
R6 `RelatedPerson.relationship` binds to this THO value set, but it was not present as a local package artifact. Expansion/comparison is needed for precise relationship-code migration.
A cross-version ConceptMap or migration table is needed to distinguish personal relationship codes from functional role codes and to handle ambiguous local codes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot rationale, or change proposal was reviewed. The report is based on package artifacts and local terminology files.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official RelatedPerson R6 change notes or rendered diff once available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No terminology server expansion was performed. The analysis compares binding metadata and local ValueSet compose definitions, but not full expansions, subsumption closure, or version-specific THO content.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run a terminology server expansion for the R4 and R6 relationship/language value sets, including `v3-PersonalRelationshipRoleType`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is `6.0.0-ballot4` and package metadata marks it not for publication. Future ballot or publication builds may adjust wording, bindings, or value sets.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the assessment against the final published R6 package.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: I did not run an official FHIR Validator instance over example resources. The validation analysis follows StructureDefinition binding strengths and FHIR conformance semantics.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Validate representative R4 and migrated R6 examples with the target FHIR Validator and terminology server configuration.
